findings.title: QoS panel per-direction queue-depth row overflows the 300px panel plate by ~130-160px - the rev columns paint unclipped onto the map
findings.verification: confirmed (mechanical geometry, no vision needed: QOS_PANEL_W=300 -> plate right edge x=312; qdx starts after the 'queue depth (bound N):' label (~154px at 14px Plex Sans) ~= x 184; each direction consumes 30 (dir label) + 3x34 (lanes) + 10 = 142px -> dir1 ends ~326, dir2 ends ~470. draw_text -> rnd.draw_text_font -> rl.DrawTextEx with NO scissor/clip (app/render/view.odin:1436). draw_qos_panel draws whenever sel_pipe >= 0 (the panel's primary state) - every panel-open frame with a selected pipe paints ~130-160px of UI past the plate onto the map. T2 goldens do not capture the panel (harness never draws it) so the defect is not canonized in goldens but is live in the shipped UI. 4 independent lenses converged.)
findings.detail: The S5 'minimal mechanical render edit' doubled the row width without widening the plate or clipping. User-visible UI garbage on a shipped HUD surface - the panel's core QoS-visibility feature.
findings.recommended_fix: Reflow within the plate: two stacked rows (fwd / rev), or compact lanes (drop the 10px gaps + narrower dir labels), or widen the plate. Add a geometry pin (the rect-math test pattern at qos_nudge_rect).

findings.title: AV-7 max-never-sum rollup (warnings pipe-congestion) is UNPINNED - a sum implementation passes the entire suite
findings.verification: confirmed by PERKINS MUTATION: replacing max(press[LO_TO_HI], press[HI_TO_LO]) with a+b passes all 276 tests (restore -> green). No test loads both directions of one bundle in the warnings fixture - test_pipe_congestion_lane_bound spawns 6 same-direction packets (max==sum there).
findings.evidence:
worst := max(press[int(bs) * PORT_DIR_COUNT + int(PORT_DIR_LO_TO_HI)],
             press[int(bs) * PORT_DIR_COUNT + int(PORT_DIR_HI_TO_LO)])
findings.detail: Spine AD-7/AV-7 ratifies max-never-sum as a reads-contract RULE the render heists build on; a refactor flipping it to sum would double-count congestion pressure in the player's face with zero gate barking. House bar: a gate that cannot be made to fail is a blocker.
findings.recommended_fix: Extend test_pipe_congestion_lane_bound (or add a sibling): load BOTH directions at different depths, pin the pipe level to the WORSE (max) port - the sum mutation must fail.

findings.title: AV-4 util MAX-over-directions form is UNPINNED in both stats and the read fn - a sum implementation passes the entire suite
findings.verification: confirmed by PERKINS MUTATION: stats.odin:233 row.util_pct = max(u_lo,u_hi) -> u_lo+u_hi passes all 276 tests. The pinned fixture's reverse port reads 0 within the window at tick 24 (the S3 re-pin comment states it), so sum==max there; port_util_pct's only assertion is the pre-traffic zero (the comment names the 'saturated reads 100, never 200' AV-4 pin but never asserts it - grep: one match).
findings.detail: AV-4 is a ratified AD-7 rule ('the MAX over directions, never Sum'); the render heists consume this reads contract. Both guard sites are unpinned - the named AV-4 gate is vacuous.
findings.recommended_fix: After the full-duplex drain fixture (both directions ~saturated for a window): assert port_util_pct==100 per direction (never a pair-sum 200) and pin a stats row where both directions are non-zero in-window so the max-form (not sum) is the unique passing implementation.

findings.title: Residency ledger regression pins MISSING for both swarm-claimed fixes (layout reset on Topology.gen + staleness fold at read) - each mutation passes the entire suite
findings.verification: confirmed by PERKINS MUTATIONS x2: (a) dropping the layout_gen==topo_gen guard from residency_layout passes 276/276 - the same-count renumber leak the swarm says it fixed ('hunter-probed at 120 phantom ticks pre-fix') would regress silently; (b) dropping the lo-bound (staleness fold) in port_residency_ticks' slot walk passes 276/276 - an idle key would read a frozen forever-stale sum, the exact defect the PR claims folds at read time. No test reads past RESIDENCY_WINDOW_TICKS or exercises a topology edit mid-history (the tx ring HAS test_bundle_tx_window_expiry_and_reuse - the residency ledger's mirror is absent).
findings.evidence:
if f.residency.keys == keys && f.residency.classes == classes && f.residency.layout_gen == topo_gen { return }  -- guard-drop mutation: PASS
if r.slot_tick[base + s] > lo && r.slot_tick[base + s] <= tick { sum += u64(r.ticks[base + s]) }  -- lo-drop mutation: PASS
findings.detail: The PR's swarm section claims both fixes as landed hardening; neither has a regression pin. The S5 mutation leg (record-pass deletion -> (b)=7 pin) covers the record path, not these two read/lifecycle paths.
findings.recommended_fix: Mirror the tx-ring's expiry/reuse test: (a) accumulate residency, topology-edit with same bundle count, assert the ledger RESETS (no phantom ticks); (b) accumulate, idle > RESIDENCY_WINDOW_TICKS, assert the key reads 0.

findings.title: Residency ledger maintains a `win` rolling-sum array NO read ever consumes - dual bookkeeping that can silently drift
findings.verification: confirmed: r.win[key] is written every packet-tick (+= 1, -= on stale fold) but the only reads are bounds checks (len(r.win)); port_residency_ticks walks the raw slots - the win VALUES are never consumed anywhere in core/ or app/.
findings.evidence:
r.win[key] -= u64(r.ticks[slot])
...
r.win[key] += 1
-- vs port_residency_ticks: sum += u64(r.ticks[base + s]) (the slot walk is the truth)
findings.detail: Dead derived state maintained per packet-tick; a bug in the win bookkeeping would be invisible to every read and every test. Either consume it (O(1) read) or delete it (ODN-18 scratch discipline).
findings.recommended_fix: Delete the win array (the slot walk is the single source) or make port_residency_ticks read it - one mechanism, not two.

findings.title: u32 wrap guard bounds ONE multiplicand: bandwidth_demand is capped 1..4096 but packet_bandwidth (the other multiplicand) has only a >0 check
findings.verification: confirmed: packet_demand_units returns u32(demand) * u32(cat.balance.packet_bandwidth); catalog bounds demand (1..4096, 'the u32 demand-total bound') but packet_bandwidth only > 0 - the product wraps for authoring-time bandwidth > 2^32/4096 = 1,048,576 (current value 120; the pace-knob comment documents 4x retunes, so the seam is authoring-reachable in principle).
findings.evidence:
return u32(demand) * u32(cat.balance.packet_bandwidth)
-- catalog: if b.packet_bandwidth <= 0 { return ... 'must be > 0' }  (no upper bound)
findings.detail: The wrap guard's comment assumes bandwidth <= 800 ('4096 x 800 = 3.3M << 2^32') but never enforces the assumption on the field it multiplies.
findings.recommended_fix: Bound packet_bandwidth at load (e.g. <= 1<<20) or compute the product in u64 and validate < 2^32 at the catalog seam.
